thesis: Mechanism: RSI(2) below 10 while price still sits above its 200-day SMA identifies a 1-3 day, statistically extreme downside spike inside an intact long-term uptrend -- forced or panicked short-horizon selling (stop-loss triggers, single-stock margin calls, index-fund rebalancing flow, overreaction to a headline) in a name whose underlying demand (consumer staples, branded pharma, integrated energy) has no reason to have changed in 48 hours. The 200-day filter is the same 'nothing structural has broken' proxy c01-meanrev used; the entry indicator is deliberately much shorter and much stricter than c01's bb_lower(20,2) so it fires on genuine short-horizon panic rather than on any garden-variety pullback, and it targets a faster, shallower bounce rather than a full band-width reversion. The counterparty is whoever sold into that 1-3 day spike without repricing fundamentals -- forced sellers, momentum-following short-term traders extending a move, or algorithmic stop cascades. My exit (close back above the 5-day SMA) sells into the snapback while it is still fresh, rather than waiting for a slower 20-day mean the position may never reach. Pre-registered failure regime: a fast, deep, *sustained* decline where the 200-day SMA has not yet turned down -- the entry keeps re-firing on 'dips' that are actually the first third of a much bigger leg down (2008's Sep-Oct acceleration is the closest historical analogue among this round's windows), and the 5-day-SMA exit and 10-day time stop do not arrive before the position is stopped out, repeatedly, until the 200-day average finally rolls over.
